correctness.rationale: The prior independent proof check stands, using Liu's sideline convention. With t=h−y>0, the two equal-side lines give r2+r3=2t/sqrt(1+h²). The triangle inequality applied to (1+x,y) and (1−x,y) gives R2+R3≥2sqrt(1+y²), with equality only when x=0 because y>0. Also −2y/R1≥−2y/t, strictly unless x=0. At x=0 the defect has numerator sqrt((1+h²)(1+y²))−h−y over t. Rationalization gives the stated numerator (hy−1)² and positive denominator. Thus equality in the stronger bound is exactly on the altitude; equality in the original inequality is at y=1/h, interior iff h>1. This is the orthocenter since the altitude from B has slope 1/h. Restoring the half-base shows its height is (BC)²/(4h_a). The proof is analytic, not a conclusion from the supplied numerical stress test.
residual_risks: The distances are to supporting lines, not to closed side segments. This proves precisely b=c with apex A, not the fixed-vertex ratio with a different choice of apex or the scalene case.
